extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, applicants, and interested parties in LPC rulemaking (people who wish to testify or submit comments)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for participating in Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) rulemaking: how hearings are held, permitted modes of testimony, sign-up and speaking rules, and the post-hearing adoption and publication timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of LPC rules PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: You can access a PDF version of the LPC Rules, effective July 25, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PDF of the currently effective LPC Rules is available for reference; use it to review the exact text of rules and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing statute: CAPA (Chapter 45)
rubrics_metrics.description: The City Administrative Procedure Act (CAPA), Chapter 45 of the New York City Charter, establishes the procedure for adopting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking follows CAPA requirements; see CAPA for statutory procedural obligations and timelines that LPC must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing requirement (Section 1043(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Section 1043(b) of CAPA, the Commission holds a public hearing in LPC’s public hearing room on the 9th Floor at 1 Center Street, New York, NY 10007, at which the public and interested parties are invited to testify in person or submit written testimony or comments on any proposed rule revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rule revisions trigger a public hearing where in-person testimony and written comments may be given; note the specified hearing location and statutory citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted modes of participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation by videoconference is also available via the Zoom teleconferencing application, which allows applicants and members of the public to participate using the Zoom app on their computer or smartphone or by telephone using a dial-in number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public may participate in-person, via Zoom (app), or by telephone dial-in. Make arrangements/confirm access method ahead of time and follow any Zoom instructions posted for the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check Hearings page for updated hearing information
rubrics_metrics.description: Please check the Hearings page on LPC’s website for updated hearing information, sign-up sheet links, the agenda and Zoom instructions, if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before attending or testifying, consult the LPC Hearings page for the latest details, sign-up links, agendas, and technical instructions; information may change between announcement and hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign-up availability and on-site sign-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public and interested parties can also sign up in the hearing room before the session begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have not pre-registered, arrive early to sign up in person in the hearing room; follow the posted sign-up procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public and interested parties... can speak for up to three minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral testimony at the hearing is time-limited (three minutes per speaker); plan remarks to fit within the allotted time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission review and potential amendment after testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing the public testimony and submitted testimony, the Commission can amend the proposed rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public and written testimony may lead to changes in the proposed rules; testimony is considered by Commissioners prior to final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final adoption process and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: A final version of the proposed rules would be presented to the Commissioners at a public meeting, where they can vote to adopt. If approved, the final rules are published in the City Record and are effective 30 days after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption requires a Commissioners' vote at a public meeting; publication in the City Record begins the 30-day countdown to rule effectiveness.
